content.rationale: The version decision's content is one machine-readable token, and this refinement makes that token a development sentinel carried in the tree between releases instead of a release value. The observation this evaluation already described — recorded token equals a pinned release value — no longer states the commitment: the decision now records no release number at all, and the release number the old observation pinned is exactly what it stops recording, so an equality against a second copy of one release string could not tell a sentinel from a release. The check therefore reads the same artifact, content.content from nodes/nlomlqum.json, and observes two properties of the one token, both stated by the decision. Shape: the token parses as a semantic version whose pre-release carries the 'dev' identifier, so a bare MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH release value fails whatever its digits — this is the half that generalizes the decision's 'no release number' beyond the single value it names, and it is why the check is not a duplicated literal. Identity: the token is 0.0.0-dev, the sentinel the decision records, so a dev-marked release core does not stand in for it. A failure names the recorded token and which property diverged. It reads no stamping surface: a surface carrying the token is a separate use of the version decision, on its own edge, and its equality to the recorded token is checked by the evaluation covering that use (E-I1a, uzwwmprz, for the manifest; pnoptpkk, for the lockfile). How a release substitutes the tagged version for the sentinel is the release step's business; this gate's subject is the token the graph records. The prerequisite is prose and the dependent is tool-checkable, the matrix's natural-to-code fidelity cell: the check translates the prose's sentinel and no-release-number claims, neither stricter nor looser.
